messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/prompt (route=promptv5-router). SLO breach detected: 5m error rate > 2.5%.
pagerduty: Paging @emily.chen (on-call)
alice.nguyen: we promoted promptv5-router canary to 20% at 14:02 UTC, started seeing timeouts around 14:09
john.patel: seeing connection resets and queue depth spikes in the router logs
alice.nguyen: log excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T14:09:12Z ERROR prompt-router promptv5 id=abc123 upstream-reset code=ECONNRESET latency=0.0
2026-03-17T14:09:13Z WARN  prompt-router promptv5 queue-depth=120 pending=98
```
alice.nguyen: leaning toward immediate flag cutoff - if we flip the ff traffic stops hitting promptv5
rebecca.cs: CS: 3 customers (ApexHealth, QuickDesk, Tutorly) reported degraded streaming/chat responses, we've opened tickets and notified them we're investigating
john.patel: agreed. Command to flip: `/ff toggle promptv5_router false --env=prod`
deploy-bot: Executing feature flag toggle: promptv5_router -> false (scope=prod)
deploy-bot: Result: success 
emily.chen: confirmed flags off, percentage routing reverted to stable v4. Monitoring metrics now
deploy-bot: Initiating rollback of prompt-service: roll to promptv4-stable (deploy job id=89f7)
deploy-bot: Rollback started; health checks scheduled
alice.nguyen: keeping watch on error rate and streaming latencies
dave.park: error rate dropping in the 1m window, tail latencies improving :thumbsup:
emily.chen: paging @john.patel for post-incident ownership and RCA follow-up
rebecca.cs: CS will send a customer-facing summary once we confirm service stable (ETA ~15m)
john.patel: taking ownership for postmortem. Initial hypotheses: regression in kernel selection / connection pooling under the new routing path. Collecting traces and heap/conn metrics now
alice.nguyen: note for postmortem: canary weighting logic didn't respect backpressure signals from the runtime; also check batching/caching params for promptv5 variant
emily.chen: oncall handoff: I'll stabilize and then pass to @dave.park for deeper digs in 1.5h. Leaving runbook link and checklist in the incident ticket
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by emily.chen
john.patel: added brief to incident board #INC-2026-113; tagging infra/serving/runtime and eng-releases
rebecca.cs: CS update sent to affected customers at 14:35 UTC — they asked for ETA on full root cause
emily.chen: marking incident contained; if any regression appears we reopen immediately
alice.nguyen: :white_check_mark: thanks everyone, good coordination
